exam.title: MongoDB Associate Developer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite is published. MongoDB recommends software-engineering experience and MongoDB training or equivalent application use. Select C#, Java, Node.js, PHP or Python, then practice BSON/document behavior, precise CRUD and aggregation results, workload-driven indexes and modeling, Atlas exploration, and the exact official-driver syntax, types, pooling, cursors and errors.

objective_coverage.objective_group: MongoDB Overview and the Document Model (8%)

review.notes: All six September 2 weighted domains are mapped through BSON/flexible-document behavior, precise CRUD and aggregation state, query-shaped indexes, workload-based modeling, current Atlas exploration, and selected-language official-driver URI/pooling/types/cursors/errors. Three application scenarios, eight authorized labs and 40 original checks are included. The public exam contract still renders, but the enrolled objective body could not be deterministically re-audited on September 7; that blocker and the dated weight baseline are explicit. OWASP NoSQL guidance adds secure application practice without being treated as MongoDB exam scope. No recalled/live item, dump or copied course content is used.

public_objective_groups.title: MongoDB Overview and the Document Model
objectives: Given differently shaped documents, identify which can coexist in one collection.

public_objective_groups.title: CRUD
objectives: Identify valid and invalid insert operations for structured documents.
Predict database state and results for document replacement and operator updates.
Select an update with upsert behavior when no matching document exists.
Select correct multi-document update and delete operations.
Predict atomic find-and-modify behavior under concurrent operations.
Select read operations for equality, arrays, embedded documents, projection, sorting, and result limits.
Trace common MongoDB Query Language and aggregation operations used to retrieve and transform data.

public_objective_groups.title: Indexes
objectives: Explain the purpose, benefits, and write/storage costs of indexes.
Select and create appropriate single-field, compound, multikey, and unique indexes for query shapes.
Interpret explain-plan evidence and identify index-supported and covered behavior.

public_objective_groups.title: Data Modeling
objectives: Given relationships and access patterns, select embedding or referencing and explain the atomicity and growth tradeoffs.

public_objective_groups.title: Tools and Tooling
objectives: Given a scenario, load Atlas sample data and use a MongoDB data exploration tool to locate a specified document.

public_objective_groups.title: Drivers
objectives: Explain the selected official language driver and how an application uses it.
Identify MongoClient URI components and connection-pooling benefits.
Identify selected-language syntax for insert, update, delete, find, and aggregation operations.
Distinguish MongoDB Query Language syntax from selected-driver language syntax.
